Given subset sum elements and a target value, each element becomes one single isolated vertex. Since no edges exist anywhere in the graph, the subgraph weight is simply the sum of all chosen vertex weights together. This crucially means a subgraph of weight T exists if and only if some subset of elements sums to T, thus proving full NP-hardness. Because the reduction from subset sum runs in polynomial time, the problem is definitely NP-hard, and combined with the complete NP membership proof, the problem is NP-complete.
